Regular Meeting – November 26, 2013

BOARD OF EDUCATION VALHALLA UNION FREE SCHOOL DISTRICT

VALHALLA, NEW YORK November 26, 2013 Board of Education Regular Meeting Members Present: LaVerne Clark, Joseph Garbus, Robert Ierace, Ronald Cavallo, Valentina Belvedere Members Absent: Alan Higgs, James Adams Personnel Present: Dr. Brenda W. Myers, Superintendent, Mrs. Christina Howe, School Business Official, Rosa Abbondola, District Clerk Call to Order:  At 7:10PM, Ms. Clark presiding at the Middle/High School Library. EXIT SIGNS ANNOUNCED TO PUBLIC PLEDGE TO FLAG I. Review and Approval of Board Agenda A motion was made by Robert Ierace and seconded by Ronald Cavallo that the board, after review, approves the agenda as presented and/or amended.  Motion passed 5-0. II. Approval of Board of Education Minutes A motion was made by Valentina Belvedere and seconded by Joseph Garbus that the minutes of the following meeting be approved as corrected or as presented: October 22, 2013 Regular Meeting November 12, 2013 Work Session November 14, 2013 Bond Referendum Motion passed 5-0. III. Acceptance of Financial Report & Budget Transfers: October 2013 A motion was made by Robert Ierace and seconded by Ronald Cavallo that the financial reports for October 2013 be approved as presented.  Motion passed 5-0. IV. Presentations • G.O. Representatives updated the Board of Education – Steven Carpenter (HS) spoke about fundraisers at High School, Kayla Greenberg (MS) spoke about “White Out” event with Westlake, Sara Bartlett & Jordan Williams (Student Council - KS) both read statements about their roles as President and Vice President of Student Council. • Megan Scalley (KS), Arisa Fourie & Rachel Ebling (MS) told stories from Tellebration and the Storytelling Club.  Next Tellebration is 12/11 at Kensico Library • Christina Howe presented a brief synopsis of the Internal Audit Report • Jon Thomas gave an overview of scheduling changes next year.  Bell schedule will change to 40 min per class, Pre-calc math will be an honors class, SAT Prep will be give after school, and AP Euro will now be available in Senior year. • Roberto Trigosso presented a change to the daily flex period in middle school.  Flex will change to a weekly class period instead of the current daily, 4 day rotation period.


<!-- Page 2 -->


Regular Meeting – November 26, 2013

V. Superintendents Report • Dr. Myers noted that the school calendar is not yet complete due to the fact that the district has not received Regents dates from SED. • Dr. Myers congratulated the board on passing the Bond Referendum and thanked the community for supporting the bond.  Paperwork has been sent to SED and we are in the queue. • Jamie Block is working on updating the Food Allergy Procedures. Ingredient lists will have to be supplied by parents who bring any food or deserts into the elementary schools.  It will be a nut free environment in both elementary buildings and there will be nut free tables at lunch time. VI. Public Comment There were no comments from the public at this time. VII. A copy of said agreements shall be incorporated by reference within the minutes of this meeting. Motion passed 5-0. 2. 6. Approval of Bond Referendum A Motion was made by Ronald Cavallo that the following resolution be adopted:

BOND RESOLUTION OF THE VALHALLA UNION FREE SCHOOL DISTRICT, NEW YORK, ADOPTED NOVEMBER 26, 2013, AUTHORIZING THE CONSTRUCTION OF VARIOUS IMPROVEMENTS TO ALL DISTRICT BUILDINGS, STATING THE ESTIMATED TOTAL COST THEREOF IS $3,658,116, APPROPRIATING SAID AMOUNT THEREFOR, AND AUTHORIZING THE ISSUANCE OF $3,658,116 SERIAL BONDS OF SAID DISTRICT TO FINANCE SAID APPROPRIATION.

Recital

WHEREAS, at the Special District Meeting and Election duly called and held on November 14, 2013, in

the Valhalla Union Free School District, in the County of Westchester, New York, the qualified voters

present and voting approved the Bond Proposition authorizing the Board of Education to construct

various improvements to all District buildings, at the estimated total cost of $3,658,116, and to levy and

collect a tax to be collected in annual installments to pay the principal of and interest on the serial bonds

authorized to be issued;

Now, therefore, THE BOARD OF EDUCATION OF THE VALHALLA UNION FREE SCHOOL

DISTRICT, IN THE COUNTY OF WESTCHESTER, NEW YORK, HEREBY RESOLVES (by the

favorable vote of not less than two-thirds of all the members of said Board of Education) AS FOLLOWS:

Section 1.  The Valhalla Union Free School District, in the County of Westchester, New York (herein

called “District”), is hereby authorized to construct various improvements to all District buildings (the

“Project”), including (i) turf field resurfacing, construction of a press box, parking lot improvements,

window and floor replacements and building security upgrades at the Valhalla Middle/High School, at the

estimated cost of not to exceed $1,990,157;  (ii) roof and ceiling replacement and building security

upgrades at the Virginia Road School, at the estimated cost of not to exceed $1,132,638; and (iii)

gymnasium air conditioning, building security upgrades and fuel tank concrete pad reconstruction at the

Kensico School, at the estimated cost of not to exceed $535,321; all of the foregoing to include the

original furnishings, equipment, machinery, apparatus and ancillary or related site work required in

connection therewith.  The estimated total cost thereof, including preliminary costs and costs incidental

thereto and to the financing thereof, is $3,658,116 and said amount is hereby appropriated therefor.  The

plan of financing includes the issuance of $3,658,116 serial bonds of the District to finance said

appropriation, and the levy and collection of taxes on all the taxable real property in the District to pay the

principal of said bonds and the interest thereon as the same shall become due and payable.


<!-- Page 4 -->


Regular Meeting – November 26, 2013

Section 2.  Serial bonds of the District in the principal amount of $3,658,116 are hereby authorized to be

issued pursuant to the provisions of the Local Finance Law, constituting Chapter 33-a of the Consolidated

Laws of the State of New York (herein called “Law”), to finance said appropriation.

Section 3.  The following additional matters are hereby determined and declared:

(a)  The period of probable usefulness applicable to the purpose for which serial bonds are authorized to

be issued pursuant to this resolution, within the limitations of Section 11.00 a. 97 of the Law, is thirty (30)

years.

(b) The proceeds of the bonds herein authorized, and any bond anticipation notes issued in anticipation of

said bonds, may be applied to reimburse the District for expenditures made after the effective date of this

resolution for the purpose or purposes for which said bonds are authorized.  The foregoing statement of

intent with respect to reimbursement is made in conformity with Treasury Regulation Section 1.150-2 of

the United States Treasury Department.

Section 4.  Each of the bonds authorized by this resolution, and any bond anticipation notes issued in

anticipation of the sale of said bonds, shall contain the recital of validity as prescribed by Section 52.00 of

the Law and said bonds, and any notes issued in anticipation of said bonds, shall be general obligations of

the District, payable as to both principal and interest by general tax upon all the taxable real property

within the District without limitation of rate or amount.  The faith and credit of the District are hereby

irrevocably pledged to the punctual payment of the principal of and interest on said bonds, and any notes

issued in anticipation of the sale of said bonds, and provision shall be made annually in the budget of the

District by appropriation for (a) the amortization and redemption of the bonds and any notes in

anticipation thereof to mature in such year and (b) the payment of interest to be due and payable in such

year.

Section 5.  Subject to the provisions of this resolution and of the Law and pursuant to the provisions of

Section 21.00 relative to the authorization of the issuance of bonds with substantially level or declining

annual debt service, Section 30.00 relative to the authorization of the issuance of bond anticipation notes

and Section 50.00 and Sections 56.00 to 60.00 of the Law, the powers and duties of the Board of

Education relative to authorizing bond anticipation notes and prescribing the terms, form and contents and

as to the sale and issuance of the bonds herein authorized, and of any bond anticipation notes issued in


<!-- Page 5 -->


Regular Meeting – November 26, 2013

anticipation of said bonds, and the renewals of said bond anticipation notes, are hereby delegated to the

President of the Board of Education, the chief fiscal officer of the District.

Section 6.  The validity of the bonds authorized by this resolution, and of any notes issued in anticipation

of the sale of said bonds, may be contested only if:

(a) such obligations are authorized for an object or purpose for which the District is not authorized to

expend money, or

(b) the provisions of law which should be complied with at the date of the publication of such resolution,

or a summary thereof, are not substantially complied with, and an action, suit or proceeding contesting

such validity is commenced within twenty days after the date of such publication, or

(c) such obligations are authorized in violation of the provisions of the constitution.

Section 7.  This bond resolution shall take effect immediately, and the District Clerk is hereby authorized

and directed to publish the foregoing resolution, in summary, together with a Notice attached in

substantially the form prescribed by §81.00 of the Law in “The Journal News,” a newspaper having a

general circulation in the District and hereby designated the official newspaper of said District for such

publication.

*   *   *

The adoption of the foregoing resolution was seconded by Board Robert Ierace and duly put to a vote on

roll call, which resulted as follows:

AYES: Joseph Garbus, Valentina Belvedere, Ronald Cavallo, Robert Ierace, LaVerne Clark

NOES: none

The resolution was declared adopted.
